# PicoCalc bouncing-block / one-paddle PONG

*README.MD file mostly generated by Anthropic's Claude AI because Thomas Dzubin hates documenting code.  LOL*

A 9x9 "ball" bounces inside a 320-wide x 256-tall playfield anchored to the
**top-left** of the 320x320 LCD. A 5x40 **white paddle** on the left edge is
moved with the arrow keys; the ball bounces off it, with a bit of "spin"
depending on where it hits. The serve is slow; every paddle hit speeds the ball
up by 10% (capped).

The ball is served from the **right wall**. Below the playfield is a two-digit
**seven-segment counter** (48 px tall, red-LED look) and, next to it, an
**MM:SS elapsed-time readout** that ticks once per second. Both blank their
leading zero (an unlit ghost digit). The counter starts at **9** and drops by
one on every miss. When it reaches **0** the game freezes; press any key to
start a new game.

Sounds (0.2 s each): **800 Hz** on a side bounce, **600 Hz** on a paddle hit,
**400 Hz** on a miss.

Controls (PicoCalc keyboard):

- **UP / DOWN** - move the paddle (tap to nudge, hold to slide; it coasts to a stop)
- **ESC** or **Q** - leave for the PicoCalc UF2 Loader menu (at any time, including the game over screen). If the game was flashed straight to the chip with no loader, it just restarts; on a PC it closes
- **~** (SHIFT + backtick) - reboot into BOOTSEL (USB mass storage) mode at any time

## Files

- `main.c` - just `main()` and the game loop
- `game.c` / `game.h` - all the helper functions: seven-segment drawing, the
  non-blocking beeper, `clampf`, and the ball serve
- `constants.h` - every tunable value and colour
- `drivers/` - `lcd.c`, `font-8x10.c`, `keyboard.c`, `southbridge.c`, `audio.c`
  (+ `audio.pio`) and headers, copied from
  [picocalc-text-starter](https://github.com/BlairLeduc/picocalc-text-starter).
  `keyboard.c` has a one-line change so held keys auto-repeat.
- `CMakeLists.txt`, `pico_sdk_import.cmake` - Pico SDK build files (the firmware build also
  copies its `.uf2` to the top level as `bouncing-block-RP2040.uf2` / `-RP2350.uf2`)
- `desktop/` - Desktop (SDL2) build for Windows and Linux: its own `CMakeLists.txt` plus a small shim of the
  driver API

## Build

Needs the Raspberry Pi Pico SDK (2.x) and the `arm-none-eabi` toolchain.

### VS Code (Raspberry Pi Pico extension)

Open this folder, "Switch Board" to **Pico**, then **Compile**. The `.uf2`
lands in `build/`.

### Command line

```bash
export PICO_SDK_PATH=/path/to/pico-sdk
cmake -B build -G Ninja
cmake --build build
```

### Windows build

The same program also runs on Windows through a small SDL2 layer in
[`desktop/`](desktop/) that stands in for the PicoCalc's LCD and keyboard and audio.
From an MSYS2 UCRT64 shell with SDL2 installed:

    cmake -S desktop -B build-windows -G Ninja
    ninja -C build-windows

Output: `bouncing-block-Windows.exe` in the top-level folder. SDL2 is linked statically,
so it is a single file with no `SDL2.dll`. `~` simply closes the program.

### Linux

The same source builds on Linux with the SDL2 development package installed
(for example `sudo apt install libsdl2-dev`). Unlike the Windows build, SDL2 is
**not** linked in statically: the program links `libSDL2` dynamically, and the
build copies that library next to the executable as `libSDL2-2.0.so.0`, where
the executable finds it through an `$ORIGIN` run-path. Keep the two files
together.

    cmake -S desktop -B build-linux
    cmake --build build-linux

Output: `bouncing-block-Linux` and `libSDL2-2.0.so.0` in the top-level folder.

## Flash

Hold **BOOTSEL**, plug the Pico into USB, copy `build/bouncing-block-<chip>.uf2` (`<chip>` is `RP2350` or `RP2040`, matching the board) to the
`RPI-RP2` drive. The board reboots and the game starts. After that, pressing
**~** (SHIFT + backtick) drops back into BOOTSEL so you can copy a new `.uf2`
without touching the board, and **ESC** or **Q** return to the UF2 Loader menu.

## Tweak

Everything adjustable is in `constants.h`:

- `FIELD_W`, `FIELD_H`, `WALL` - playfield size and border/inset thickness
- `BALL_SIZE`, `SERVE_SPEED`, `SPEED_GAIN`, `HSPEED_MAX`, `VY_MAX` - ball size,
  serve speed, per-hit speed-up, speed cap, spin cap
- `PADDLE_W`, `PADDLE_H` - paddle dimensions
- `PADDLE_ACCEL`, `PADDLE_FRICTION`, `PADDLE_VMAX` - paddle feel / speed
- `BEEP_MS`, `TONE_MISS`, `TONE_HIT`, `TONE_WALL` - sound effect length and pitches
- `SEG_W`, `SEG_H`, `SEG_T`, `DIGIT_GAP`, `COLON_W` - seven-segment digit geometry
- `SCORE_X`, `TIMER_X`, `BOTTOM_Y` - positions of the two bottom readouts
- `START_LIVES` - counter start value
- `FRAME_MS` - frame delay
- `COLOR_BG`, `COLOR_BALL`, `COLOR_PADDLE`, `COLOR_BORDER`, `SEG_ON`, `SEG_OFF` - colours

MIT, see `LICENSE`. The vendored drivers from `picocalc-text-starter` by Blair Leduc keep their own license (see the `LICENSE` file that comes with them). They are his code of 2026-10-18 (commit `85a002e`) with two local changes: `lcd_putstr()` in `lcd.c` cuts a string
off at the right edge of the display, and `keyboard.c` treats a held key as a press, so that the arrow keys auto-repeat.
